decisions.paths: Skills must not hardcode vendor paths. Declared in AGENTS.md when the repo declares one; otherwise a fixed documented default. Discovery/heuristic scanning rejected: nondeterministic across sessions.
decisions.docs-superpowers-rename: Executed 2026-09-04: docs/superpowers/{specs,plans} -> docs/{designs,plans}; 34 citations across 15 files. Two references intentionally left in docs/reviews/2026-07-05-telemetry-plan/ where a reviewer quotes the old path while arguing against it.
decisions.installer-destructive: Measured 2026-09-04: `skills experimental_install` rm -rf's each skill dir and copies from unpinned upstream HEAD. skills:setup guard changed from completeness-count to existence so the destructive path is unreachable once a tree exists.
decisions.retired: find-skills (vercel registry surface, zero inbound refs) and using-superpowers (Skill-tool bootstrap; premise fails in an auto-injecting harness). tdd folded into test-driven-development, which keeps the name 7 cross-references point at.
decisions.namespace: superpowers:<name> prefixes stripped to bare names. A stale vendor prefix resolves to no skill silently.
decisions.structure: Companion files grouped by role: references/ (docs an agent reads), prompts/ (subagent templates), scripts/ (executables), examples/. Previously four skills held 3-6 files flat in the skill root.
decisions.cross-skill: Skills never assume another skill is installed. Frontmatter `uses:` declares name + source (github repo) so a harness can resolve or fetch; body text degrades to a manual fallback when the skill is absent.
decisions.provenance-paths: Local companion regrouping (references/, prompts/, scripts/) changed paths that upstream still holds flat. Each file records upstreamPath when the local path differs, so status is recomputed against snapshot bytes rather than assumed from the local name.
decisions.naming: Skill names use gerund/verb-first form per writing-skills:217 and Anthropic's authoring guide ('we recommend gerund form'). Exceptions kept verbatim: test-driven-development and subagent-driven-development name established methodologies an agent searches by name; systematic-debugging already reads verb-first.
decisions.skill-split: writing-skills covered authoring AND adversarial testing in 1873w. Split: writing-skills keeps structure/naming/layout, testing-skills owns baseline runs, pressure scenarios, and loophole closing. They reference each other via uses:.
decisions.routing: Sibling skills covering the same trigger must each state the discriminator and name the alternative. executing-plans and subagent-driven-development both key on subagent availability; using-git-worktrees and dispatching-parallel-agents explicitly disclaim plan execution.
decisions.uses-graph: Every skill named in another skill's description, body, or companions is declared in that skill's uses: block. Bare sibling names in prose are backticked so a name is visually distinct from an ordinary word.
decisions.uses-is-agent-facing: Verified against skills@1.5.23 dist/cli.mjs: the installer parses only name and description; 'uses' appears nowhere. uses: survives installs because unknown keys are ignored, not because anything acts on it. It is agent- and human-facing metadata, so every imperative handoff in the body must also state a fallback.
decisions.standalone: Verified by enumeration, not sampling: all 24 declared dependency edges were exercised with the target skill absent, across four isolated installs. Zero dead ends. 8 edges carry an explicit fallback; 16 are informational cross-references ('Related skills' entries, scope notes) that strand nobody. Only imperative handoffs require a fallback.
decisions.metrics: Corpus at 8ff325d: 24 skills, 42 companions, mean 817w, max 1562w (writing-skills), 6 skills over 1000w. Earlier summaries reported mean 809w / max 1422w - those were measured before the 'Declaring cross-skill dependencies' section was added in the same commit (eda7812), so they understated writing-skills by 140w.
decisions.diagrams: Diagrams are mermaid fences, not graphviz. graphviz needs a `dot` binary that is not installed here, so the 11 dot fences were unrendered source text; mermaid renders natively in GitHub, VS Code, and agent UIs. TheGrid's docs/conventions/diagramming.md already mandates mermaid, and diagramming-with-mermaid explicitly defers format choice to the consuming repo. 9 fences converted and validated with mermaid.parse; one deliberately-bad example left as dot; graphviz-conventions.dot and render-graphs.js deleted as dead.
decisions.mermaid-validation: Validated against mermaid 11.17.2: Pass A mermaid.parse under jsdom 9/9; Pass B mermaid.render in real Chromium 9/9 with no error-SVG and min SVG 13,895 bytes (real diagrams, not stubs). Both passes teeth-checked 5/5 against unclosed brackets, misspelled type, ':: ' in state label, ';' in sequence message, malformed ER cardinality. Silent-pitfall scan clean; parenthesised labels confirmed verbatim via getDiagramFromText. Note: this repo pins no mermaid dependency and has no CI check, so GitHub's renderer version may differ.

decisions.rule-ownership: Each rule lives in exactly one skill; siblings state a hand-off rather than restating. Contrast splits deliberately: building-accessible-interfaces decides whether a ratio is required, building-color-systems measures the rendered pair and changes values. Typography owns text rendering, writing-interface-copy owns the words. Hand-off lines added to building-accessible-interfaces, designing-component-systems and following-repo-ui-conventions so ownership survives the corpus growing.
decisions.authoring-conventions: Adopted 2026-09-06 from jakubkrehel/skills AGENTS.md: calibration (state how hard to press), detection-pattern mistake tables (left column an observable symptom, not a restated principle), and one-home-per-rule with explicit hand-off lines. The SKILL.md template block and the creation checklist were updated in the same pass so the template does not teach prose for a section the rule requires as a table. Rejected his no-trigger-list description philosophy: it contradicts this corpus's routing constraint that descriptions carry a 'Use when' trigger.
decisions.vendor-snapshot-removed: Removed 2026-09-06. vendor-snapshot/local (584K) was byte-identical to the pre-consolidation tree already in git history - verified by comparing blob sha256 at 2e3c5aa~1. vendor-snapshot/upstream (568K) was verified fetchable on demand at each pinned SHA with matching sha256. What is load-bearing for re-merge is the pinned SHA plus the recorded hash, not the bytes. Cost of the removal: a re-merge now needs network, and a force-pushed or deleted upstream is unrecoverable - accepted, since the pins are public repos and the recorded hashes still prove drift.
decisions.scope: This repo consolidates cross-cutting craft knowledge that multiple third-party sources each state slightly differently - accessibility, layout, typography, color, copy, review and process workflow. Vendor tool skills (framework, design-tool, CLI and API surfaces) are NOT forked here: they change when the vendor's product changes, so the vendor owns that truth and they are installed from the publisher. Forking one buys a maintenance burden and guarantees staleness.
decisions.registry-survey: Surveyed ui-skills.com/skills/registry.txt (289 entries, ~80 sources) on 2026-09-06. Found via a browser crawl of jakub.kr after reading rendered text repeatedly failed - the catalog indexes both sources previously supplied (jakubkrehel, leonxlnx), so those were leaves of a tree not yet examined. Verdicts: the overwhelming majority are VENDOR TOOL SKILLS (figma 16, antfu 19 framework skills, vuejs-ai 8, mengto 18 GSAP/three.js, vercel next-*, microsoft playwright, remotion) - rejected by scope, not quality: those belong to their publishers and are installed, never forked. Adopted MECHANISMS ONLY from two: vercel-labs/web-interface-guidelines (an org-backed rule list; extracted form affordances, motion, compositor, CLS, safe-area, i18n and native-theming rules into the five existing owner skills) and jakubkrehel/oklch-skill (confirmed the perceptual-lightness and hue-drift rules already carried in building-color-systems; its channel-range table and APCA thresholds were already covered by references/notation-and-gamut.md and references/measuring-contrast.md). Rejected as skills: ibelick/baseline-ui (deslop UI - overlaps cleaning-ai-slop and following-repo-ui-conventions), anthropics/frontend-design and the generative aesthetic skills (prescribe a visual style that following-repo-ui-conventions forbids inventing), cursor/unslop (prose humanizing, not UI), the accesslint set (a hosted rule engine - a tool to run, not knowledge to hold), mattpocock/* process skills (this corpus already forked what it wanted at 3cca18b). No third-party skill was installed or vendored as a result of this survey.
decisions.clip-path-article: jakub.kr/work/clip-path-buttons found by browser crawl and absent from /api/rss, so an RSS-derived inventory missed it. Content is one sentence plus an interactive demo, no extractable rules. Rejected.
decisions.absent-records: Six records describe skills deliberately not present in .agents/skills/: context7-cli, firecrawl and web-search are vendor surfaces installed from their publisher rather than forked; find-skills is retired; tdd was folded into test-driven-development; using-superpowers was retired as its Skill-tool bootstrap premise fails in an auto-injecting harness. Each carries presentInTree:false and an empty files map, so a drift check does not report intentional absence as missing files. Their upstream pins are kept so the decision stays auditable.
decisions.description-conventions: Audited 2026-09-06 against the rules the corpus actually codifies in writing-skills (third person, trigger phrase, name matches directory) rather than invented ones. Three violations fixed: brainstorming was second person with no trigger ('You MUST use this before...'), finishing-a-development-branch and writing-plans each addressed the reader as 'you'. writing-skills also gained a writing-plans entry in uses:, since it names that skill in prose while teaching the convention. Note: an earlier pass flagged em dashes and curly quotes across 40 files; that standard is NOT codified anywhere in this repo and those files were left alone. Style rules that no document states are not violations. Follow-up: writing-skills' checklist said descriptions must start with 'Use when...' while its own prose and the README said only 'states when to use'. Two skills legitimately open with 'Use before' (brainstorming, using-git-worktrees) because they run ahead of their trigger rather than in response to it, so the checklist and README were aligned to that reality instead of forcing 25-of-27 phrasing onto two accurate descriptions. Rejected in the same pass: a claim that the corpus bans hyphens in descriptions in favour of em dashes. No such rule exists anywhere; the only hyphen rules in writing-skills govern the name field.
decisions.jakub-kr-site-sweep: Browser-driven sweep of jakub.kr on 2026-09-07, after the user asked whether earlier passes had missed anything. They had. Prior surveys read 11 pages found by BFS link-crawling; the sitemap lists 16 and the union is 15 real pages (~13,900 words, 79 headings). Five substantial rule-bearing pages had never been read at all: /components/oklch-colors, /work/gradients, /work/drag-gesture, /work/motion-gestures, /work/shared-layout-animations. Worse, /writing/details-that-make-interfaces-feel-better had been mined for ONE section (shadows-instead-of-borders, now designing-component-systems:85) while its ten sibling sections were skipped - the crawl was section-blind, extracting only where a rule matched something already being looked for. NINE mechanisms adopted across four skills, each verified absent first: image edge outline (designing-component-systems), staggered composite entrance + quieter exits + gesture commit threshold + no fling momentum on committing gestures + staged progressive reveal (building-accessible-interfaces), polar-space hue detour + gradient midpoint hints (building-color-systems), grayscale font-smoothing with its contrast tradeoff (refining-typography). The font-smoothing rule was deliberately written CONDITIONAL rather than as the article states it: the source presents antialiased as a straight improvement, but it overrides a user's system rendering preference and thins strokes, so it was tied to the existing weight floor. Rejected by scope: Motion-library implementation guides (drag/layoutId/FLIP internals - vendor tool material, same rule that rejected the 289-entry registry), /writing/less-is-more (essay on working with agents; its restraint thesis is already reviewing-for-bloat), /skills index page (11 published skills - install, never fork). Measurement note: token-level greps produced FOUR false readings this session (text-wrap, tabular-nums, gesture 'threshold' matching 'snapshot', 'exit' matching 'complexity'). The corpus states rules stack-agnostically by design, so coverage must be checked by concept, never by CSS token.
decisions.jakub-kr-rejection-ledger: Complete per-page verdict for jakub.kr after a full-text browser pass on 2026-09-07 (15 pages, 78,617 chars, every page read end to end). ADOPTED (15 mechanisms): /writing/details-that-make-interfaces-feel-better -> image inset outline, staggered entrance, quieter exits, grayscale smoothing (conditional). /components/oklch-colors + /work/gradients -> polar hue detour, midpoint hints. /work/drag-gesture -> commit threshold, no fling momentum, staged progressive reveal. /work/shared-layout-animations -> one identity per state, continuity-excludes-entrance, interpolate-don't-swap. /work/motion-gestures -> press cancels on travel, subtle focus feedback, scroll-reveal must not gate existence. REJECTED WITH REASON: (1) /work/clip-path-buttons, /work/infinite-card-stack, /work/interfere-logo, /work/shader-playground - demo pages, 444-725 chars, one-line descriptions and live controls, no stated rule to extract. (2) /writing/less-is-more - essay on restraint when working with agents; thesis already held by reviewing-for-bloat ('complexity grows faster than capability') and its agent-workflow principles are about the reader's judgement, not interface knowledge. (3) /work/using-ai-as-a-design-engineer - personal tooling workflow (Cursor modes, Figma MCP, context7, model choice, subscription-gated rule sets); its one portable artifact is the /deslop command, which this corpus already carries as cleaning-ai-slop. (4) /skills index - 11 published skills to install via npx, not fork; same scope rule that rejected the 289-entry ui-skills registry. (5) Motion library mechanics throughout - layoutId, AnimatePresence, FLIP internals, drag props, while- prop API: vendor implementation detail that belongs to Motion's docs. (6) / homepage - bio and index, no rules. CORRECTION TO PRIOR PASS: /work/shared-layout-animations and /work/motion-gestures were first rejected wholesale as 'Motion-library guides' after reading only the opening ~40% of each. Both carried portable constraints in the unread remainder; six rules were recovered on the full read. Rejecting a page on a partial read is the same error as the section-blind extraction recorded in jakub-kr-site-sweep. UNVISITED BY DESIGN: interfaces.dev (paid magazine), oklch.fyi (separate tool site) - external properties linked from the homepage, out of scope for this repo's corpus, noted here so a later pass knows they were seen and skipped rather than missed.
decisions.jakub-kr-full-text-audit: Read-coverage audit on 2026-09-07 prompted by the user asking directly whether every article had been read in full. It had not: measuring displayed spans against page lengths showed 19,772 chars unread across five of eight articles - /work/gradients entirely (10,259, only four extracted sections had ever been displayed, never the contiguous page), /writing/less-is-more 5,356, /work/drag-gesture 2,448, /components/oklch-colors 1,226, /work/motion-gestures 483. Reading every gap produced ONE further adoption: frequency governs whether to animate at all, derived in less-is-more from a context menu opened 200x/day at 300ms costing a minute daily. That page had been rejected twice as 'an essay' on the strength of its intro and its closing principles list, while its middle carried a concrete, quantified motion rule - the third time a partial read produced a wrong verdict. REJECTED after full read, with reason: gradients' linear/radial/conic tour, direction keywords, size keywords, position, hard stops, repeating gradients and the four-layer diamond recipe are CSS syntax reference, which this corpus does not teach (MDN owns it) and which is why the same page's interpolation-space and midpoint-hint material WAS adopted - those are decisions, not syntax. oklch tail is a tool plug (oklch.fyi) and a Hacker News note. drag-gesture tail is Motion component code; its one portable detail, that gesture-revealed actions carry onFocus so they stay keyboard-reachable, is already covered by 'All functionality must be reachable and operable by keyboard' at building-accessible-interfaces:45. motion-gestures tail is the article's own conclusion. Measurement note: this session token greps produced a FIFTH false positive - 'frequency' matched 'frequent commits' and 'frequently-loaded', nearly suppressing the one real gap. Every coverage claim in this corpus must be confirmed by reading the matched line, never by hit count.
decisions.jakub-kr-extraction-completeness: Extraction-completeness audit on 2026-09-07, prompted by the correct observation that comparing read-spans against my own dump proves only that the extractor was consistent, not that it captured everything. Three independent channels were tested against the live DOM. (1) HEADING/LENGTH PARITY: re-fetched all 15 pages with networkidle2 plus a full scroll to trigger in-view content, compared every h1/h2/h3 and total length against the stored dump - delta 0 on every page, zero missing headings. This is weak evidence alone, since both sides use innerText. (2) RSC PAYLOAD: document.textContent runs 10-30x larger than innerText (384KB vs 11.5KB on the details article), so the Next.js __next_f payload was mined for prose. First attempt returned 0 sentences on all 15 pages - FALSE ZERO, caught by a teeth check that confirmed the payload demonstrably contains a known visible sentence while my regex found only ONE quoted run, because the payload is an escaped JS string literal and the whole blob matched as a single run. After unescaping, 25 unrendered prose strings surfaced across the 15 pages: all are the shared 404 template ('This page doesn't exist') plus per-page meta descriptions. No article content is server-serialized but unrendered. (3) TOGGLE-HIDDEN PANELS: innerText only captures the active tab, so every tab/radio/switch/button on the seven interactive pages was clicked and text re-collected. Only the details article yielded anything - 11 blocks, all Tailwind class strings from the Motion/CSS code-sample switcher on the icon-animation section, plus one demo headline. No prose rule was hidden behind any toggle. CONCLUSION: the corpus-relevant text of jakub.kr is fully captured; 16 adopted rules stand. METHOD NOTE: this was the SIXTH false-negative measurement of the session and the only one caught by a deliberate teeth check rather than by contradiction with a known fact. Any harness that reports zero must first be shown capable of reporting non-zero.
decisions.details-article-per-claim-audit: Per-claim audit of /writing/details-that-make-interfaces-feel-better on 2026-09-07. Earlier passes checked this article ONE RULE PER SECTION; splitting it into its 11 sections and enumerating every distinct claim inside each produced 25 claims, of which three were absent. ADOPTED: (1) interruptibility is a property of the technique - a transition interpolates toward the current target so a new intent retargets it mid-flight, while a keyframe sequence runs a fixed timeline and cannot change course; the corpus already required interruptibility but never said what delivers it, so the requirement had no actionable half. (2) optical alignment - centre by eye not arithmetic, icon-side padding trimmed against a text label, and fix it in the asset rather than per usage so it travels with the icon. (3) hover elevation - deepen the existing shadow rather than swapping recipes, since changing layer geometry mid-interaction reads as the element resizing. REJECTED: word-level stagger of a heading, a marketing flourish already bounded by the corpus rule that caps composite entrances at semantic chunks. MEASUREMENT: 'optical alignment' had read as covered(4) in an earlier probe; every hit was the opsz optical-size font axis in opentype-and-variable-fonts.md, unrelated to visual centring. Seventh false positive of the session, and the reason this audit was run per-claim rather than per-section.
decisions.thegrid-ui-md-and-lawsofux: Verdict on the two remaining sources, 2026-09-07. (A) /workspaces/TheGrid/docs/conventions/ui.md is TheGrid's OWN repo-specific convention file - it mandates Tailwind utilities and @apply composition and says of itself 'intentionally concise and repo-specific'. It is a consumer of this corpus, not a source for it: harvesting its styling section would breach following-repo-ui-conventions:19, which forbids introducing a styling stack the target project has not already chosen. Verified zero occurrences of 'tailwind' or '@apply' anywhere in the corpus, so nothing from that section leaked. Its two portable layout rules were already present (building-responsive-layouts:33 fallback trigger must not appear while its panel is unavailable; :34 navigation collapses before wrapping into a half-state). (B) lawsofux.com, surveyed in full: 30 laws, not the ~24 assumed - 19 actionable, 7 mixed, 4 descriptive. LICENSE IS CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (Jon Yablonski), which permits citation and quotation but FORBIDS distributing adapted or remixed versions of its text; a rewritten rule set derived from its wording would violate the ND term. This constrains how the site may ever be used here. All seven laws named as candidates were checked against their source definitions and every checkable one is ALREADY held, independently stated: Jakob's at following-repo-ui-conventions:48, Hick's/Choice-Overload at :51, Serial Position at :50, Fitts's at building-accessible-interfaces:75-76, Goal-Gradient at :120, Zeigarnik at :71 and :122, Doherty across improving-web-performance:78 and the immediate-feedback rule. Aesthetic-Usability REJECTED as descriptive: all three of its takeaways describe user perception, and 'aesthetically pleasing' carries no threshold a reviewer could check. NOTHING ADOPTED from either source. MEASUREMENT: an initial regex reported Hick's and Jakob's ABSENT - eighth false negative of the session. Both were present at following-repo-ui-conventions:48 and :51, missed because the corpus states laws by their mechanism and never by name. Searching for a law's NAME cannot establish whether its RULE is held.
decisions.final-corpus-review: Full-corpus review on 2026-09-07 across four parallel reviewer passes (UI contradictions, clarity/bloat, process consistency, structure/graph) plus a mechanical near-duplicate detector over all 1,061 rule lines. TWELVE defects fixed. CONTRADICTIONS: (1) building-accessible-interfaces' own manual checklist said 'verify non-essential animation is removed' while its rules at :96 and :98 require a reduced variant and a near-zero duration rather than removal - the checklist would have failed compliant code, and I introduced it myself when adding those rules. (2) measuring-contrast.md called APCA 'the better default for design decisions' while both building-accessible-interfaces:21 and the outranking following-repo-ui-conventions:66 mandate WCAG AA; APCA is now the instrument and WCAG the gate, stated in all three places. (3) subagent-driven-development routed to executing-plans on 'parallel session' while executing-plans:3/:23 and writing-plans:153 both define it as the no-subagents inline fallback; SDD now routes on subagent availability. ONE-HOME-PER-RULE: reserve-space and no-injection lived in full in both building-responsive-layouts and improving-web-performance and had ALREADY DRIFTED ('result counts' vs 'ads, async result blocks'), which is exactly the failure the README rule predicts; overlay-shell stability had three homes. Ownership resolved per the README table, duplicates replaced by hand-offs, and the two missing uses: edges declared. following-repo-ui-conventions restated five accessibility rules its own boundary paragraph assigns to siblings, one near-verbatim; replaced with a hand-off that keeps what the skill uniquely adds, namely that an accessibility rule outranks a contradicting house convention. DEAD REFERENCES: requesting-code-review's closing line pointed at a path missing its prompts/ segment; systematic-debugging pointed at a 'Phase 4.5' that exists nowhere in the skill or its references, so the 3-failures rule is now self-contained. GRAPH: improving-web-performance and reviewing-for-bloat had zero uses: edges and are now connected; reviewing-for-bloat assigned 'fix now' dispositions without ever naming cleaning-ai-slop, which cleaning-ai-slop:15 calls its corrective counterpart. README: three false claims corrected - every arrow declared in uses: (the dashed verifies-edge is not), 'takes no inbound edge' while the diagram drew one into it, and 'owned:false are vendor surfaces tracked here' when all six records are presentInTree:false and three are retired or merged rather than vendor. STRUCTURE: handing-off-work was 104 words with no title and no headings, the only skill violating the template writing-skills mandates; restructured with mechanisms attached to each rule rather than padded. REJECTED: a claimed contradiction between subagent-driven-development:139 and executing-plans:72 over starting on main - both forbid it, the SDD line sits under a '**Never:**' header that my own detector had stripped. Also rejected the claim that requesting-code-review must declare two siblings in uses:, since it names only one and in unhyphenated prose, not as a skill reference.
decisions.motion-skill-split: building-accessible-interfaces reached 12.5KB, tied for largest in the corpus, because this session added roughly thirteen rules to it and most were motion craft rather than access constraints. Classifying all eighteen rules in its motion section split 7 craft / 10 accessibility / 1 shared, and the craft seven have no accessibility failure mode at all: frequency budgets, continuity identity, continuity-excludes-entrance, interpolate-vs-swap, the transitions-vs-keyframes mechanism, staggered entrances, quieter exits. DECIDING EVIDENCE: the README ownership table already scoped this skill to 'motion REQUIREMENTS', not motion craft, so the seven violated a boundary the corpus had already drawn. No existing skill owned motion craft - designing-component-systems covers APIs, composition, state ownership and token consumption, and absorbing motion there would have repeated the mistake one skill over. Created animating-interface-motion (28th skill) holding the seven, with a Role section stating that building-accessible-interfaces owns what motion must satisfy and outranks it. Two requirement/mechanism pairs were kept intact rather than split across the boundary: the interruptibility REQUIREMENT stays in the accessibility skill with a hand-off naming where the technique lives, since separating a requirement from its mechanism is the exact defect fixed in systematic-debugging's dangling Phase 4.5 pointer earlier in this same review. Result: 12.5KB to 10.6KB, no rule lost, no rule duplicated, verified by asserting each moved rule is present in exactly one of the two files. README table row reworded from 'motion requirements' to 'motion constraints' and the composition graph gained motion with edges a11y -> motion and motion -> a11y.
decisions.rust-corpus: Added 2026-09-07: five Rust skills as original text restating mechanisms from MIT-licensed sources, not forked. Skills: writing-idiomatic-rust (ownership, clones, fallibility, error-type design, iterators, dispatch), reviewing-unsafe-rust (what each unsafe operation requires, soundness preconditions, FFI), writing-async-rust (cancellation, state across await points, blocking, task lifetime), hardening-rust-supply-chain (dependency policy, lockfiles, advisories), speeding-up-rust-builds (critical path, crate graph, dev profiles). Licensing: actionbook/rust-skills (1.4k stars, the obvious candidate) has NO LICENSE file and the GitHub API reports license:null despite a README MIT badge, so its text carries no grant; its adoptable content is also coupled to a router/hook plugin system. Sources used had their MIT text read in-tree: apollographql/skills, mohitmishra786/low-level-dev-skills, Rust-Coding-Guidelines/rust-coding-guidelines-zh. writing-async-rust has no upstream: no surveyed source covered cancellation semantics. Rejected by scope: actionbook m01-m15 meta-cognition (routing scaffolds, not checkable rules), actionbook domain-* and tool wrappers (crate recipes and vendor CLI wrappers), actionbook's Deprecated table ('std::sync::Mutex -> parking_lot' with no reason or version), apollo's Quick Reference (bare assertions; reasons live only in the chapters), apollo-router-plugin-creator (product surface), trailofbits rust-review (orchestration harness stating no rules), rust-no-std (substantive but no consumer here). Verification: claims that compile were compiled. 10 cases under rustc stable including two negatives that must fail (Vec<T> to &[T]; non-Send held across an await). That sweep found one defect - the ownership section claimed a &str parameter accepts a String, which is E0308; deref coercion covers &String. Structural gates (frontmatter, graph parity, hashes, mermaid) cannot see a false claim, so tool and language facts are verified against primary sources instead.
decisions.rust-tool-facts: Verified 2026-09-07 against primary sources (cargo-deny 0.20.2 and cargo-audit 0.22.2 books plus their source; the Cargo Book, rustc book, and Rust blog). Corrected five defects the structural gates could not see. (1) Neither cargo-deny nor cargo-audit supports an ignore expiry: IgnoreId takes only id + reason and finalizes with deny-unknown-fields, so `expires` is a parse error, and cargo-audit's ignore is a bare Vec<Id>; the skill had recommended recording an expiry. (2) 'Set each policy to deny' was incoherent - vulnerabilities, unlicensed, and non-allowed licences are hardcoded Severity::Error with no key, and unmaintained takes a Scope enum, not a lint level. (3) wildcards defaults to allow, not warn; the book's prose is a doc bug contradicted by source and by the maintainers' deny.template.toml. (4) The bin/lib lockfile split was officially retired 2023-08-29 and cargo new no longer ignores lockfiles for libraries. (5) rust-lld has been the default on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu since 1.90, so -fuse-ld=lld is stale there; also debug=1 is 'limited' not line-tables-only, lto=false is not 'off', codegen-backend is nightly-only, and opt-level>=2 on dependencies stops monomorphised generics being shared across crates. Also corrected: the crate-graph section had led with 'break circular dependencies first', but cargo rejects package cycles at resolution (measured: `error: cyclic package dependency`, exit 101), so that build cannot exist. Replaced with the real constraint - a split must follow a one-way dependency, and the only legal cycle is through dev-dependencies, which costs build ordering under cargo test. Version anchors added to the skills themselves, not just this record: the cargo-deny lint table is marked 'Verified against cargo-deny 0.20.2' and carries a note that the schema moves (unmaintained became a scope; vulnerability, severity-threshold and unlicensed were removed), the expiry finding names cargo-deny 0.20.2 / cargo-audit 0.22.2, and the debug ladder names the 1.71 MSRV for the string forms. Without an anchor a reader cannot tell a schema change from an error in the skill, and because these configs reject unknown keys a stale key fails the build rather than being ignored.
decisions.rust-async-runtime-scope: Verified 2026-09-07 against std docs, tokio 1.53.1, async-std 1.13.2, smol 2.0.2 / async-task 4.7.1, plus direct measurement. writing-async-rust originally stated tokio behaviour as universal. Findings: (1) DIVERGENCE - dropping a task handle detaches under tokio and async-std but CANCELS under smol and anything on async-task, which marks Task #[must_use = "tasks get canceled when dropped"]. Measured: identical spawn-drop-wait shape runs under tokio and never runs under smol. The skill had asserted the tokio behaviour as universal, which is inverted for half the ecosystem. (2) 'Cancellation safety' is tokio's own term, defined on its select! docs; std and futures-rs do not use it, and the per-API verdicts are tokio's about tokio's APIs. (3) Tokio's own Mutex docs say 'Contrary to popular belief, it is ok and often preferred to use the ordinary Mutex from the standard library in asynchronous code', contradicting the skill's blanket 'needs an async-aware lock'. (4) A non-Send value across an await is compiler-level, not runtime-level, and under spawn_local it compiles and runs correctly - measured; the skill had wrongly attached a deadlock to it. The real deadlock is a blocking guard held across an await on a single-threaded runtime, measured as a total hang in which a 400ms tokio::time::timeout never fired because the timer could not run. (5) block_in_place is multi-threaded-only and panics on a current-thread runtime; std provides no offload facility at all. Language-level claims (lazy polling, cancel-by-drop, auto-trait derivation) are now separated from runtime-specific ones, and versions are anchored in the overview. Lock guidance sharpened after review: the two directions have different force and were measured separately. std Mutex by default is a preference (tokio's own docs). An async lock when the guard spans an await is a REQUIREMENT: a std guard is not Send, so under tokio::spawn it is a hard compile error ('future cannot be sent between threads safely', measured exit 101), while the identical code under spawn_local compiles and runs (measured exit 0) and fails instead as the runtime hang. Same rule, different enforcement; the skill now states both directions in the body, checklist and anti-patterns.
decisions.rust-unsafe-verification: Verified 2026-09-07 against stable Rust 1.90 by compiling every checkable claim; reviewing-unsafe-rust had shipped with no verification pass. Confirmed: all five classic capabilities are genuinely gated (E0133 for deref/unsafe-call/mutable-static/union-field, E0200 for unsafe trait impl, each proven by a without-unsafe negative that fails and a with-unsafe positive that compiles); safe rules stay in force inside an unsafe block (a use-after-borrow is still E0502); Send/Sync are auto-derived, a manual impl without unsafe is E0200, and a raw-pointer struct is not auto-Send (E0277). Corrected: (1) 'exactly five capabilities' is wrong - inline assembly is also gated by E0133, and in edition 2024 attributes such as #[no_mangle] require an unsafe(...) wrapper, so five is the historical framing not the current count; the overview asserted this too. (2) 'A Rust panic unwinding into foreign frames is undefined behaviour' is outdated - since Rust 1.81 it aborts (measured: exit 134 SIGABRT). The advice to catch at the boundary stands; the stated mechanism did not. Strengthened with measurement: repr(Rust) genuinely reorders a u8,u32,u8 struct to offsets 4/0/5 against repr(C)'s 0/4/8 and is smaller (8 vs 12 bytes); a crate with an out-of-bounds read and a double-&mut passes cargo test 2/2 green while cargo miri test reports 'error: Undefined Behavior' and exits 1, and clippy on the same UB exits 0 with zero warnings - the skill's claim that a clean lint run is no evidence about unsafe correctness is now demonstrated rather than asserted. Also noted that miri halts at the first violation, so a clean rerun does not prove there was only one.
decisions.rust-build-measured-from-practice: Updated 2026-09-07 from a real workspace's .cargo/config.toml and Cargo.toml (TheGrid, 24 crates, nightly-2026-08-18) whose settings carry their own measurements. Two corrections and two additions. CORRECTION 1: the skill said rust-lld is the default since 1.90 and treated that as toolchain-wide; it is per-target. Verified with `rustc --print link-args` on this box: the host aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu target links via plain `cc` with no fuse-ld flag, and `fuse-ld=lld` appears only when -Clinker-features=+lld is passed explicitly. The 1.90 change landed for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu only. CORRECTION 2: two paragraphs contradicted each other after the first edit - one saying lld is already on, the next saying 'if you do switch to lld'. Resolved into a single per-target rule. ADDITION 1: the lld thread-oversubscription trap, which the skill omitted entirely and which inverts the advice. lld defaults to one thread per core PER LINK while cargo links concurrently; measured on a 12-core box relinking 33 test binaries, GNU bfd 38.3s, lld --threads=1 13.1s, lld default threads 120-150s - the fast linker was 4x SLOWER than the one it replaced until capped. ADDITION 2: debug-info numbers with a verified backtrace-parity claim - debug=true 29.2s, line-tables-only 10.1s, debug=0 6.6s, with 41 resolved frames under both true and line-tables-only and 0 under debug=0, so the 2.9x costs debugger variable inspection rather than backtraces; plus the per-session CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=true override and the [profile.bench] exemption that profilers need. Follow-up 2026-09-07 after a reviewer questioned whether the rust-lld default claim and its anti-pattern were true at all. Verified against the 1.90.0 release notes, PR #140525, the rustc book, and compiler source; plus measured locally. Three further corrections. (a) The default is narrower than 'x86_64 since 1.90': it is applied via a bootstrap env var (CFG_DEFAULT_LINKER_SELF_CONTAINED_LLD_CC) only for x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and only in the toolchains rustup distributes, so a distro-built rustc may not have it. (b) -Clinker-features=+lld is unstable on EVERY target including x86_64 and errors without -Zunstable-options - measured here as 'error: `-C linker-features=+lld` is unstable'; only the -lld opt-out is stable, and only on x86_64. The skill had presented +lld as an ordinary knob. (c) The anti-pattern 'Adding -fuse-ld=lld where rust-lld is already the default' was WRONG: the rustc book states 'If the user also passes a -Clink-arg=-fuse-ld=$value, both will be given to the linker driver but the user's will be passed last, and would generally have priority over rustc's', so it is redundant and harmless rather than conflicting. Replaced with the real hazard - using a -fuse-ld override as an opt-out instead of the supported -Clinker-features=-lld, noting that rustc's old-GCC retry strips only the exact string -fuse-ld=lld so a differently-spelled override survives a retry meant to drop it.

upstreamRetrieval: Upstream bytes are fetched on demand at the pinned SHA rather than vendored into this repo: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/<repo>/<sha>/<path>. Every upstream file records its sha256 here, so a drift check verifies the fetched bytes without trusting the network. A vendor-snapshot/ directory previously held these bytes; it was removed as bloat (1.2MB, 134 files) after verifying the fetched blobs are byte-identical to the snapshot and that vendor-snapshot/local duplicated content already in git history at f7b6fdf.
